text: Cleanside Road and Mendelssohn Street are local residential streets where residents have raised ongoing concerns about speeding, road safety, and the need for stronger traffic calming measures. These streets are used daily by residents, pedestrians, cyclists, families, seniors, children, and other vulnerable road users travelling through the neighbourhood. Through consultation and flyer drops conducted by the Councillor’s office on the affected streets, a majority of residents expressed support for the installation of speed humps. Residents noted that speeding vehicles create unsafe conditions, reduce comfort for people walking or cycling, and impact the overall safety and livability of the neighbourhood. The Scarborough Community Council: 1. Authorized the installation of traffic calming (nine speed humps) on Cleanside Road, between Warden Avenue and Pidgeon Street, generally as shown in Attachments 2 and 3, Drawing Nos. TC-712 and TC-712-1, to the letter (May 28, 2026) from Councillor Parthi Kandavel. 2. Authorized the installation of traffic calming (four speed humps) on Mendelssohn Street, between Roper Road and Deans Drive, generally as shown in Attachment 5, Drawing No. TC-714, to the letter (May 28, 2026) from Councillor Parthi Kandavel. 3. Authorized the installation of traffic calming (one speed hump) on Mendelssohn Street, between Deans Drive and Cleanside Road, generally as shown in Attachment 4, Drawing No. TC-713, to the letter (May 28, 2026) from Councillor Parthi Kandavel.
